impact.affected_asset: Availability of a service or application that accepts incoming COSE messages through go-cose and indexes a map with the decoded content-type header.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a relying application to process a COSE content-type header with an unhashable decoded value and panic when it uses that value as a map key.
impact.security_effect: Application panic and denial of service under the reported relying-application usage pattern.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies an incoming COSE message whose content-type header is decoded from attacker-controlled data.

The audit reports that content-type (label 3) is defined as a text string or unsigned integer, but go-cose validates alg and crit rather than content-type, allowing its type contract to remain unenforced.
A relying application uses the decoded content-type value as a Go map index while expecting a string or integer; an unhashable supplied value reaches that map-key operation.
The unhashable map key causes the relying application to panic, producing an application-dependent denial of service.

failure.operation: Go map indexing with an unhashable decoded content-type header value

primary_invariant.kind: protocol header type contract at the decoding boundary
primary_invariant.statement: The decoded COSE content-type header must be a text string or unsigned integer before applications consume it as a typed header value.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reviewed library did not validate content-type even though it validated alg and crit, so an attacker-controlled value outside the specified content-type domain could be delivered to a relying application.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit gives a concrete conditional panic scenario and recommendations, but this bundle does not provide the audited historical headers.go revision, a malicious COSE fixture, a stack trace or observed test run, an invariant-restoring patch, regression test, or confirmed affected-version range. The panic depends on a downstream application using the decoded content-type value as a map key.

remediation.invariant_restored: Commonly used COSE headers are checked during unmarshalling for their specified type and semantic consistency, so content-type values delivered to applications conform to its registered value domain.
